chunks: And it is narrated from Yāsir al-Khādim, who said:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: 'Can the month of Ramaḍān be twenty-nine days?' So he said: 'Indeed, the month of Ramaḍān never decreases from thirty days, ever.'

key_terms.أَبَداً: ever; an emphatic expression of permanence
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the one being asked
key_terms.الْخَادِمِ: the attendant or servant; title identifying Yāsir
key_terms.تِسْعَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ: twenty-nine, referring to the possible number of days
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ يَوْماً: thirty days, the number stated in the reply
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the month of fasting
key_terms.يَاسِرٍ: Yāsir, the narrator transmitting this report

ai.seo_question: Can the month of Ramaḍān ever be only twenty-nine days according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Yāsir al-Khādim asking Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام whether the month of Ramaḍān can be twenty-nine days. The Imam عليه السلام replies that Ramaḍān does not fall short of thirty days, presenting a ruling related to fasting and the length of the sacred month.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2044 - It is narrated from Yasir Al-Khadim, who said:

"I asked Al-Ridha (as): 'Can the Month of Ramadan ever be 29 days?'
Imam (as) replied: 'The Month of Ramadan is never less than 30 days.'"
